ledger_entries.claim: dependencyMeasure formula's own proven properties (bounds, antisymmetry, self-zero)

rust_side.note: independent hand-transcription of the literal formula, NOT wired to any production wasm4pm code path

ledger_entries.explicit_non_claim: This does NOT claim correspondence to wasm4pm::causal_graph::CausalRelation.strength. That field is a DIFFERENT formula: unsigned usize in [0,1000], with negative heuristic measures explicitly clamped to 0.0 via `.max(0.0)` before scaling (confirmed by direct read of build_causal_heuristic). Clamping a signed measure to zero before an affine rescale destroys the antisymmetry dependencyMeasure's own proof depends on -- these two are not the same claim under any honest normalization.
ledger_entries.method_note: bounds/antisymmetry/self-zero checked exactly (integer cross-multiplication, not float epsilon-tolerance) over ab,ba in [0,50] -- an honest finite check, not a proof of the universally-quantified ℕ statement.

ledger_entries.claim: W4PM-LEAN-GALL-024: what IS true of the clamp/rescale that separates dependencyMeasure from CausalRelation.strength (closing the 016 gap by characterizing the lossy transformation itself, not by re-claiming the original antisymmetry)

central_theorems_meaning.clampedMeasure_add_swap_eq_abs: clampedMeasure(ab,ba) + clampedMeasure(ba,ab) = |dependencyMeasure(ab,ba)| -- the magnitude of the original signed measure survives the clamp IF both directions are kept; this is the precise sense in which the clamp is lossy-but-not-destructive-of-everything.
central_theorems_meaning.clampedMeasure_mul_swap_eq_zero: clampedMeasure(ab,ba) * clampedMeasure(ba,ab) = 0 -- the two clamped directions can never both be positive, formalizing that wasm4pm's real output (post-threshold) contains at most one of the (a,b)/(b,a) CausalRelation entries for any pair, never both.

rust_side.note: exact-rational transcription of the PRE-rescale clamp only (max(dependencyMeasure(ab,ba), 0)), matching causal_graph.rs build_causal_heuristic line 177's `.max(0.0)`. Does NOT transcribe the subsequent `* 1000.0` cast to usize or the `>= threshold` filter -- those are separate, still-uncharacterized lossy steps (see scope boundary below).

ledger_entries.still_not_claimed: This does NOT restore or approximate dependencyMeasure_antisymm for CausalRelation.strength -- the sign is still genuinely lost per-direction; only the PAIR of both directions together recovers the magnitude, and wasm4pm's real output structure (a flat Vec<CausalRelation>, threshold-filtered) does not guarantee both directions are retained or even computed together downstream. This also does NOT characterize the `* 1000.0` -> usize rescale/cast step (a second, separate lossy transformation -- rounding via `as usize` truncation) or the `>= threshold` filter, both of which remain uncharacterized in Lean. A future checkpoint would need to formalize those two steps to close the gap fully to the literal `CausalRelation.strength` field.
